overall: The AG found the Haverhill School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing and voting on a policy not listed on its March 14 notice, but the violation was cured on April 11; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly discussed and voted on a policy at its March 14 meeting that was not listed on the meeting notice, which only listed a general policy subcommittee update.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law as alleged when it discussed specific policies during its March 14 meeting without listing those policies on the meeting notice, but that its subsequent remedial action cured the violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the March 14 notice violation was intentional; the AG considered whether the Committee acted knowingly under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: We have not previously warned the Committee about the violation found here, nor do we find other evidence of an intent to violate the Law. Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law ordered; the Committee cautioned that similar future conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar conduct in the future may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
